page: OVHcloud r3-512 is a memory-optimized server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, translating to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a local 400 GB NVMe SSD, and the network configuration delivers a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in multi-threaded operations and memory bandwidth. The server achieved a PassMark CPU score of 94,314.31 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 194,535.72, both placing in the top 10% of tested hardware. Memory performance is characterized by a cached read-only small block bandwidth of 8,439.52 GB/sec and a PassMark memory score of 3,020.92. For database workloads, the instance processed 134.58 million Redis SET operations per second and scored 31,390.6 on PassMark database operations, demonstrating high efficiency for memory-bound applications.

While multi-threaded and memory-intensive tasks perform exceptionally well, single-core performance is more moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,902.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 29.15 GB/sec. The lack of hyperthreading ensures dedicated physical resources but limits concurrent thread scaling beyond the 64 physical cores. This hardware profile is highly suited for large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
